decisive_items: thin-walled (5–15 μm), pauciseptate hyphae with minimal branching
numerous thick-walled ovoid sporangia (5–20 μm) that stained strongly with PAS, GMS, and Giemsa
response.rationale: Histopathology shows angioinvasive, pauciseptate, minimally branching broad hyphae with sporangial-type cells and vascular thrombosis, the characteristic tissue pattern of mucormycosis. Other fungal or nonfungal alternatives do not explain this combination of morphology and angioinvasion.

rejected.why: Cutaneous lymphoma is contradicted by documented angioinvasive microbial structures and positive fungal stains; skin lesions and CLL history are nonspecific.
Neutropenia and fever explain the immunocompromised setting but do not account for the biopsy-proven hyphae, sporangia, and angioinvasion.
Aspergillosis is an angioinvasive mold but expected narrow septate acute-angle branching hyphae; the findings of pauciseptate hyphae and sporangia are contradictions.

Entomophthorales is a zygomycete but the prominent angioinvasion, vascular thrombosis, and necrotic clinical course are more characteristic of Mucorales; R5 only supports sporangia without the decisive angioinvasive hyphal pattern.
